subject: Discovery Recap & Next Steps — Redwood for ACME Enterprise
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Michaels <jordan.michaels@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0500
Subject: Discovery Recap & Next Steps — Redwood for ACME Enterprise

Hi Jordan — thanks again for meeting earlier today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) Key pain points you described
- Latency spikes on peak inference workloads impacting customer-facing search and chat.
- High per-token cost vs. expected volume growth (engineering has to throttle).
- Lack of predictable routing/fallback for multi-region customers.

2) Current stack / what you’re using today
- Inference: in-house endpoints on GCP (NVIDIA A100) + custom batching middleware.
- Data: customer prompts stored in internal DB, partial KV cache in Redis.
- Security: internal vendor questionnaire + SOC2 Type II required for new vendors.

3) Success criteria (what ACME will evaluate)
- 90th p95 latency under 250ms for 2k token median payloads for search flows.
- 30–40% reduction in per-token inference cost (measured over 1 month pilot).
- Seamless private deployment option for regulated vertical customers.

4) Procurement & decision process (as discussed)
- Procurement lead: Priya Sahu (cc’d).
- Security review: Amit Rao (security) will run vendor questionnaire & require SOC2 summary.
- Target decision window: 4–6 weeks pending security/commercial alignment.

5) Proposed next steps (our ask)
- Redwood to share: short sales deck + SOC2 summary + initial pilot pricing (attached).
- Align on pilot scope (traffic %, models, runbook) — propose 6-week pilot with measurable QoQ.
- Schedule a 30–45m procurement + security sync next week to walk through vendor Qs and procurement timeline.

Attachments: redwood-sales-deck.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf, pricing-pilot-quote.xlsx

If you can confirm the procurement stakeholders and whether the proposed 4–6 week decision window looks right, we’ll lock in the pilot scope and get a calendar invite out.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Jordan Michaels <jordan.michaels@acme.com>

Cc: Priya Sahu <priya.sahu@acme.com>, Amit Rao <amit.rao@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap & Next Steps — Redwood for ACME Enterprise

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few points from our side and adding procurement context so we can operationalize: 

- Pain & goals: yes, that matches what we discussed. Priority is stabilizing customer-facing latency and reducing variable spend.
- Procurement timeline: security questionnaire first (aim to complete in ~2–3 weeks), then procurement working group (we typically meet weekly — next committee is Dec 8).
- Budget guardrails: engineering has indicated an initial pilot budget in the $200k–$350k annualized range; any pilot pricing should be scoped to show delta vs. current spend.
- Contracts: we will typically require a short pilot SOW + PO for the pilot; full commercial negotiation  (T&Cs) happens after successful pilot outcomes.

Amit — I’m cc’ing you for the vendor questionnaire. I’ve attached our standard vendor security Qs for your convenience (acme-vendor-security-questions.pdf).

Would like to schedule the procurement/security sync next Tue or Wed afternoon (CST) — either 11/24 or 11/25 works for Priya and me.

I’ll also loop in our data-platform lead (will confirm name) if the pilot involves KV cache or streaming telemetry.

Thanks — Jordan

Attachment: acme-vendor-security-questions.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Michaels <jordan.michaels@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priya Sahu <priya.sahu@acme.com>, Amit Rao <amit.rao@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:35:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap & Next Steps — Redwood for ACME Enterprise

Jordan — perfect, thanks for the clarity. Quick follow-up and proposed procurement guardrails from Redwood to make the vendor review simpler: 

- Docs we’ll provide today: SOC2-summary.pdf (one-pager) and an initial pilot pricing spreadsheet (pricing-pilot-quote.xlsx).
- Pilot proposal (high level): 6-week pilot, dedicated pool for ACME (isolated tenancy), rollout on a single region to validate latency & cost metrics. Goal: demonstrate >=30% cost reduction vs. current baseline while keeping p95 latency under 250ms.
- Commercial guardrails: for pilot we propose a capped spend not to exceed $60k for the 6-week period (we can convert to a time-boxed SOW + PO). If pilot meets success criteria, we’ll escalate to a 12-month committed capacity conversation (we can propose committed discounts in that phase).
- Security/contract asks: we can complete the vendor questionnaire quickly — Amit, will your team accept the SOC2 one-pager and a short security kickoff call, or do you need the full SOC2 report and an NDA before we proceed?

Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll upload the two docs referenced above (attached).
2) Schedule a 30–45m sync with Priya + Amit + our security lead (Vivek) on 11/24 @ 1:00pm CST or 11/25 @ 2:00pm CST — which works?
3) If agreed, Redwood will produce a 1-page SOW for the pilot + capped spend clause and send to Priya for PO routing.

If that timeline works, I’ll send a calendar invite and draft SOW by EOD today.

Best,

Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf, pricing-pilot-quote.xlsx
